mechanisms.name: Print-first, silhouette-second naming
mechanisms.description: Every swim product title is 'Print Name' + silhouette: 'Burning Blue' Triangle Front Tie Top, 'Burning Blue' High Cut Cheeky Bottoms, 'Burning Blue' Double String Top. The same print name is reused verbatim across every top and bottom in that print, and the Color option value equals the print name.
mechanisms.why_it_works: Shoppers scanning a grid can see at a glance which pieces belong together without a set product, and the silhouette suffix tells them the cut before they click.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Title pieces as 'Sunchild Triangle Top', 'Sunchild Mesh Bottom', 'Moonchild Bandeau Top', and 'Bella Classic Top'/'Bella Classic Bottom'. Keep the print or Classic name identical across the pair so 16 SKUs read as a small number of families.

mechanisms.name: Mega menu split by piece and fabric family, then silhouette
mechanisms.description: The Swim menu has five columns: One Pieces, Prints Tops, Printed Bottoms, Solid Tops, Solid Bottoms. Each column lists silhouettes (Triangle Front Tie, Double String, Ruffled Up Underwire, Ruched Bandeau; Cheeky, Full, Thong, Side Tie).
mechanisms.why_it_works: It resolves the two questions a bikini shopper asks first (print or solid? top or bottom?) inside the menu, and exposes coverage names before any page loads.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Swim menu with four columns: Print Tops (Triangle, Bandeau), Print Bottoms (Triangle, Mesh), Classics Tops (Bella, Bali, Sara, Marina), Classics Bottoms. Add a fifth entry 'Build a set' that lands on a filtered collection.

mechanisms.name: Coverage encoded in the product name and first line of copy
mechanisms.description: Bottoms are named by coverage: High Cut Cheeky, High Cut Full, High Cut Thong, Side Tie. The description opens with position and coverage: 'Ultra-high cut cheeky bottoms, meant to be worn on your high hip.' and 'Fuller coverage version of original cheeky bottoms for shy bum.'
mechanisms.why_it_works: It removes the need to open a size guide to learn how much a bottom covers, and lowers return risk from coverage surprises.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Rename bottoms with a coverage word (e.g. 'Sunchild Cheeky Bottom', 'Marina Moderate Bottom', 'Moonchild Mesh Full Bottom') and open every description with one sentence on where it sits and how much it covers, in Piura's own voice.

mechanisms.name: Three-sentence spec description: adjustability, lining, origin
mechanisms.description: Descriptions are consistently short and structured, e.g. 'Adjustable triangle cups with strings that tie at neck and back. Double lined. Made in Portugal.' Tops state closure type (clasp hook, tie closure, removable straps); bottoms state wear position.
mechanisms.why_it_works: A fixed template makes 100+ SKUs feel curated and lets shoppers compare pieces quickly; the lining and origin lines do the premium signalling instead of adjectives.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Adopt a fixed template per piece: one line on adjustability (ties, sliders, removable pads), one on lining/fabric, one 'Designed in Miami. Made in Peru.' Keep it to three sentences.

mechanisms.name: Faceted filters with a Print facet and per-size availability
mechanisms.description: Collection filters: Price range, Availability (In stock/Out of stock), Size XS-XXL, Color (12 values), Print (Animal, Floral, Paisley, Solid, Stripes, Tie Dye etc). Sort includes Best selling and Date new-to-old. Sizes show as unavailable per variant on the PDP.
mechanisms.why_it_works: Filtering by size first hides what a shopper cannot buy, and a Print facet mirrors how the brand's own catalogue is organised.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Filters: Piece (Top/Bottom), Family (Sunchild, Moonchild, Classics), Silhouette (Triangle, Bandeau, Mesh), Size S-XL, In stock. With 16 pieces, filters can be always-visible chips rather than a drawer.

mechanisms.name: Two-accordion PDP with explicit, numeric policy wording
mechanisms.description: PDP order is title, price, shipping note, color, size, variant dropdown, add to cart, description, then two accordions: SIZE & FIT and Delivery & Return Policy. Policy copy uses numbers: 'Store Credit or Exchange within 10 days', ships '2-5 business days', made-to-order 'up to 2-5 weeks', 'SALE merchandise is final sale'.
mechanisms.why_it_works: Keeps the buy box above the fold and concentrates all risk-reducing information in two predictable places with concrete numbers instead of vague reassurance.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Same skeleton, but fill the Size & Fit accordion with a real S-XL chart (bust, underbust, waist, hip) and a model-size line, which Heavy Manners lacks. Keep shipping and returns to three numeric sentences.

mechanisms.name: Drop-time announcement as the only urgency device
mechanisms.description: The announcement bar reads 'AMERICAN SUMMER 7/3 @ 3PM' and the homepage has a single CTA 'Discover new arrivals'. No discounts, low-stock counters, reviews, or free-shipping bars were observed anywhere.
mechanisms.why_it_works: Scarcity comes from a calendar, not from markdowns, which protects price integrity and gives the newsletter a concrete reason to exist.

mechanisms.name: Quick variant entry from the card
mechanisms.description: Product cards use a 'Choose options' button instead of a plain link, and switch to a 'Sold out' state when no variant is available.

mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Add a size-chip quick-add (S M L XL) on hover or tap on each card, and show 'Sold out' or 'Notify me' on exhausted pieces. Pair this with a 'Add matching bottom' link on the top's card, which Heavy Manners does not do.

mechanisms.name: Shop-by-silhouette and shop-by-coverage sub-navigation
mechanisms.description: The Swimwear mega-menu splits into Style (Tops, Bottoms, One Piece), Shop by silhouette (Bandeau, Halter, Triangle, Underwire, Scoop; Bikini Briefs, Thongs, Side Tie, Medium Coverage) and Color, each as its own collection URL. Bottoms collection intro frames the range as 'From cheeky to classic'.
mechanisms.why_it_works: Swim shoppers self-select by support and coverage before print. Naming coverage in the nav removes the need to open each PDP to learn what a bottom covers.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: A three-column swim menu: By piece (Triangle Tops, Bandeau Tops, Mesh Bottoms, Classic Bottoms), By print (Sunchild, Moonchild, Classics), By coverage (Cheeky, Medium, Full). With 16 pieces each column is 3-4 links, so it stays scannable.

mechanisms.name: Card = style name + family subtitle, one card per colorway
mechanisms.description: Each product card shows a title ('Halter Tosca'), a one-line collection subtitle ('So Chic'), price, badge and a size dropdown. Every colorway is a separate card rather than a swatch row, so the grid reads as a wall of colors.
mechanisms.why_it_works: Shared style words and shared colorway names let a shopper visually match a top and bottom across cards without a set page. Subtitle line carries the family so the title can stay short.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Title = piece name (Bella Top, Sara Bottom), subtitle = print family (Sunchild / Moonchild / Classics), one card per print. Use the same print name on the paired top and bottom so pairing is obvious in the grid.

mechanisms.name: Size selector on the collection card
mechanisms.description: Collection and homepage cards carry an XS/S/M/L size dropdown directly on the card, letting a shopper pick a size before entering the PDP; sold-out sizes are marked.
mechanisms.why_it_works: Cuts one page load per item for repeat buyers building a top-plus-bottom pair, and exposes size availability at grid level.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Add an S/M/L/XL quick-select on cards with immediate add-to-bag; grey out sold-out sizes. Since tops and bottoms are separate, this lets a shopper add both from one grid view.

mechanisms.name: Bundle builder promoted inside the grid
mechanisms.description: 'Build Your Bikini' is linked in the Swimwear menu and also appears as a promo tile inside the bikini product grid with the copy 'save 10% off your dream bikini'. Lingerie mirrors this with 'Create Your Set'. (The builder page itself is JS-rendered and its steps were not observed.)
mechanisms.why_it_works: The incentive is placed where the pairing decision happens (the grid), not only on a separate page. A percentage-off frames separate top/bottom pricing as a set without forcing a set SKU.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: A 'Pair a top + bottom, save 10%' tile every 8 cards, plus a two-step builder (choose top, choose bottom, any print mix). Piura's $42-$49 pricing makes the set-discount math simple to show live ('$91 → $82').

mechanisms.name: Fit-fact-first product description with model block
mechanisms.description: The PDP 'Description & Fit' accordion is open by default and leads with construction: wireless, double-lined, fully adjustable straps, front clasp, and an explicit bust-range statement 'suited to both small & fuller busts'. A model block lists height/bust/waist/hips and 'Model wears: XS'. A 'Fit Calculator' link sits above the variant selectors.
mechanisms.why_it_works: Support and adjustability are the main uncertainty for a triangle top bought online; stating them in the first two lines reduces returns and pre-empts size questions.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Standardize a fit block for all 16 pieces: lining, padding (removable or not), tie/adjustable points, coverage level (cheeky/medium/full), bust range, plus model stats and 'Model wears S'. Put a size-guide link above the size buttons, not in the footer.

mechanisms.name: Category-tabbed new-arrivals carousel on the homepage
mechanisms.description: Homepage 'NEW ARRIVAL' block has three tabs (Swimwear, Lingerie, His & Hers) that swap the product carousel; a 6-icon category quick-nav row sits above it.
mechanisms.why_it_works: One module serves multiple audiences without stacking three carousels; the icon row gives a second, faster entry point than the header.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: A single carousel tabbed Sunchild / Moonchild / Classics, and a 4-icon quick row (Tops, Bottoms, Sets, Classics). With 16 pieces, tabs prevent an empty-feeling homepage while still showing everything above the fold on desktop.

mechanisms.name: Threshold shipping with cart progress and installment line
mechanisms.description: Announcement bar states free US shipping at $150; the slide-out cart shows 'You're $150.00 away from free shipping' with separate standard/express targets. PDP shows an Afterpay line '4 interest-free installments of $14.75' under the price.
mechanisms.why_it_works: Progress messaging turns a single top purchase into a nudge toward adding the bottom; the installment line lowers the perceived price of a set.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Set the free-shipping threshold just above one piece (e.g. $75) so any top+bottom pair qualifies, and show the progress line in the cart drawer. Add a Shop Pay/Afterpay line under PDP price.

mechanisms.name: Review count at title level plus photo reviews with distribution
mechanisms.description: The PDP shows '4.5 stars, 484 reviews' next to the title, and a Judge.me widget lower down with a star-distribution bar (79% five-star) and customer photos.
mechanisms.why_it_works: Fit confidence for swim comes from seeing real bodies in the piece; the distribution bar makes the score credible rather than a bare average.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Use a review app that captures 'fits true / runs small' and the reviewer's usual size alongside photos; show count next to the title and a fit-consensus bar ('82% say true to size'). Skip celebrity/press strips.

founder_facts.fact: "Growing up in Miami, my family spent almost every weekend at the beach, so I practically grew up in a bikini."
"My favorite bikinis were always the ones my grandma would bring me from Peru. They were flattering, unique, and unlike anything I could find in the U.S."
"Most styles felt too bulky or simply weren't my style, so I always found myself ordering swimwear from overseas. That's when I knew one day I wanted to create my own."
"Years later, after building a following on social media and helping promote so many other brands, I realized it was finally time to bet on myself."
"I saved up the money I earned bartending and poured everything into starting Piura, despite having no idea what I was doing. I just knew the only way to make my dream happen was to start."
"Piura is a coastal city in northern Peru known as the 'City of Eternal Heat.' Since my bikinis were inspired by Peru and originally made there, the name felt like the perfect fit."

"To me, Piura represents warmth, the ocean, and that endless summer feeling I wanted the brand to capture. It reminds me of where I come from while representing the life I've always loved, living by the water. The name always felt like it was meant to be."

"Inspired by my roots in Peru and life in Miami, Piura became more than a swimwear brand. It's a celebration of endless summers, iconic coastlines, and the confidence that comes from putting on a bikini you truly feel amazing in."
"My hope is that every woman who wears Piura feels confident, beautiful, and ready to collect memories and embrace every adventure."

mechanisms.name: Coverage as a first-class shopping facet
mechanisms.description: The Swim mega-menu has a dedicated Coverage column (Teeny, Cheeky, Classic, Full) alongside silhouette columns, and each bottom carries a tag like "Control Type: Classic Coverage" that also appears in body copy ("classic coverage for just the right amount of comfort").
mechanisms.why_it_works: Coverage is the single biggest anxiety when buying bottoms online. Making it a nav facet and a product attribute lets a shopper self-select before seeing a single product and reduces returns.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: With only 16 pieces, Piura does not need a mega-menu, but every bottom (mesh, triangle-set bottoms, Bella/Bali/Sara/Marina) should carry one plain-language coverage label in its own words (e.g. a three-step scale) shown on the card, in a filter chip on the collection page, and in the fit line on the PDP. Use Piura's own vocabulary, not Teeny/Cheeky/Classic/Full.

mechanisms.name: One-line fit spec with support tier and adjustability
mechanisms.description: Every top style in the fit guide gets a support tier ("Minimal Support", "Medium Support") plus adjustability facts ("Fully adjustable", "Ties at back for adjustability", "Removable cups"). On the PDP this collapses into one bullet line: "Triangle top • Ties around neck and back • Removable cups • Model is wearing a size small".
mechanisms.why_it_works: It answers support, adjustability and cup questions in under 15 words, scannable above the fold, without a paragraph.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Give each of the 16 pieces a fixed-format fit line: silhouette • support tier • adjustability points • lining/cups • model size. Triangle tops and bandeaus get different support tiers; mesh bottoms state lining. Same line on the card hover state or under the title on mobile.

mechanisms.name: Model measurements with bust cup and reviewer sizing metadata
mechanisms.description: PDP states "Model is wearing a size small • Model measurements: Height 5'8", Bust 34B, Waist 25.5", Hips 36.5"". Reviews show verified-buyer badges with reviewer height and size tried, plus a 4.7/5 rating, 90-review count, star breakdown and "92% would recommend"; the review summary surfaces that sizing runs small.
mechanisms.why_it_works: Shoppers triangulate their own body against the model and against reviewers of similar height/size, which is the closest substitute for trying on.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Publish model height, cup and size worn on every PDP in S-XL. When collecting reviews, ask for height and size purchased and display them. Even 5-10 reviews per piece with sizing metadata beats none. Add a one-line honest note like "Sunchild triangle top runs small in the cup; size up for D+" if data supports it.

mechanisms.name: Print name as the pairing key for separates
mechanisms.description: Tops and bottoms are separate $95 products whose titles share the print suffix ("Gia Triangle Top - Sand Dunes Stripe Crepe" / "Elle Tie Side Bottom - Sand Dunes Stripe Crepe"), the top's gallery shows the model in the matching bottom, and the bottom's copy says it is "made to complete your favorite bikini set". Colorway siblings are grouped by a YGroup tag and shown as a named "Fabric" selector linking to sibling pages.
mechanisms.why_it_works: The print becomes the mental unit of the outfit; the shopper lands on either half and immediately knows what completes it without a bundle widget.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Name every piece "[Style] [Silhouette] - Sunchild" / "- Moonchild" / "- [Classic color]", shoot each top with its matching bottom, and add a "Pairs with" row under the buy box linking the other half with its price and a combined total (e.g. $42 + $49). Piura can go further than the reference: an explicit two-item add-to-cart for the pair, which Vitamin A does not offer on separates.

mechanisms.name: Sets sold as a single SKU with simplified sizing
mechanisms.description: The Coast Cotton line is sold as a "Bikini Set" product at $240 with only two sizes (XS/S, M/L) and "Sold as a set" in the description, while the printed line stays as separates in XS-XL.
mechanisms.why_it_works: A set SKU removes the pairing decision and halves the size choices for a stretch fabric, lowering friction for gift buyers and first-time customers.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Offer the Sunchild and Moonchild triangle sets as an optional set SKU with a small saving next to the separates, keeping S-XL. Keep separates for mixed sizes. Mesh bottom + bandeau top could be a second set option.

mechanisms.name: Homepage as a category router, not a product grid
mechanisms.description: The homepage shows zero product cards. Order: hero with one CTA, one-sentence mission line, four category tiles each with an "Explore" button, sale, sustainability, brand story, journal, loyalty. Product cards live only in collections.
mechanisms.why_it_works: Each section has one job and one CTA, so the page reads as a series of decisions rather than a catalog, and it stays premium because nothing competes with the imagery.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: With 16 pieces, route by print and by half: three tiles (Sunchild, Moonchild, Classics) then two tiles (Tops, Bottoms), each with a single button, one line of copy, and a Miami/Peru maker line where Vitamin A puts its sustainability line. Keep the full grid one click away.

mechanisms.name: Threshold shipping and first-order capture in the announcement layer
mechanisms.description: Announcement bar rotates "Complimentary Shipping on Orders $150+ | Use Code: SHIPFREE" with two other messages; footer/newsletter offers "Enjoy $50 Off Your First Order"; mega-menu includes a price-anchored "Under $135" collection; "Notify me when available" captures email on sold-out sizes.
mechanisms.why_it_works: The shipping threshold is set just above a top+bottom pair, nudging a second piece; the email captures turn out-of-stock and first visits into a list.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Set free shipping just above one pair (e.g. two pieces, around $90) so the bar itself says "add a bottom". Use a modest first-order incentive, a "Under $45" or "Complete pair under $95" link, and a back-in-stock email on every S-XL size button.

mechanisms.name: Silhouette-based taxonomy in the nav
mechanisms.description: Tops are listed by silhouette (Triangle, Halter, Bralette, Bandeau, Cropped) and bottoms by silhouette (High Leg, Tie Side, Hipster, High Waist) in separate mega-menu columns; product tags mirror this ("Suit Type: Triangle Top", "Suit Type: Side Tie Bottoms").
mechanisms.why_it_works: Shoppers think in shapes before prints; separating silhouette from print lets both be browsed independently.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Piura's range collapses to Tops: Triangle, Bandeau; Bottoms: Tie-side, Mesh, Classic cut. Expose these as filter chips on one collection page rather than a mega-menu, and tag products so a chip plus a print chip (Sunchild / Moonchild / Classics) filters the 16 pieces instantly.

mechanisms.name: Coverage and silhouette as first-class filters
mechanisms.description: Collection filter groups are named by fit intent, not just attributes: "Coverage - Tops" (Bandeau, Bralette, Triangle, Underwire, Halter, Tankini, One Piece) and "Coverage - Bottoms" (Adjustable, Cheeky, Modest, Medium), alongside Size, Colors, Printed, Fabric. Filters are powered by Shopify tags such as filter_triangle, filter_medium, filter_tops, filter_xl.
mechanisms.why_it_works: Swimwear shoppers decide on cut and coverage before print. Naming the filter "Coverage" answers the anxiety question directly and lets the shopper self-segment in one tap.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: With 16 SKUs Piura does not need a full filter panel. Use a single chip row on the shop page: Triangle / Bandeau / Mesh for tops, Cheeky / Moderate for bottoms, plus Sunchild / Moonchild / Classics. Tag each SKU with silhouette and coverage so the chips and the product card label come from the same data.

mechanisms.name: Coverage baked into the product title

mechanisms.why_it_works: The title alone tells the shopper the piece type, the coverage level, and the print, so grid cards need no extra labels and search/SEO gets the cut keyword.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Adopt the pattern with Piura's own names: "Bella Triangle Top / Sunchild", "Bali Cheeky Bottom / Moonchild", "Marina Bandeau Top / Black". Keep the slash separator idea only if it fits Piura's type system; the mechanism is style + cut + piece + print in a fixed order.

mechanisms.name: Fixed four-block PDP description template
mechanisms.description: Each description has the same skeleton: one hook paragraph that ends with a pairing sentence; "Details:" (fabric percentages, cut, hardware such as "Tri-slot hook for custom fit"); "Size & Fit:" ("Runs true to size." plus a named model with height, bra size, waist, hips and the size she wears); "Shipping:"; "Returns:". Pre-order ship dates are inserted at the top of the same block.
mechanisms.why_it_works: A predictable structure lets a returning shopper scan to the block they care about (usually Size & Fit) and gives every SKU the same trust signals without new copywriting each drop.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Write all 16 PDPs from one template: hook + "Pairs with" line, Details (Peruvian fabric, lining, padding, tie/clasp), Size & Fit (true-to-size note + one model stat line per print, S-XL), Shipping, Exchanges. Store Details/Size & Fit as metafields so the layout can render them as accordions on mobile.

mechanisms.name: Reciprocal pairing copy plus a shared set tag
mechanisms.description: Tops and bottoms are separate SKUs, but every top ends with "Pair with the Kate bottoms" and every bottom with "Pair this with the Quinn top". Each family shares a Shopify tag ("kate set", "quinn set"). The PDP then shows a "Want More" carousel of cards with image, title, print, price, optional "NEW" badge and an "ADD TO BAG" button.
mechanisms.why_it_works: Separates-only pricing keeps the entry price low while the pairing line and set tag steer the shopper to the second piece, and add-to-bag on the carousel removes a page load from the second conversion.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Give each Piura pair a set tag (e.g. sunchild-triangle-set, bella-set). On every PDP render a "Complete the set" module that shows the exact matching piece first with an add-to-bag button and the combined price, then other pieces in the same print. This is the biggest lever for a brand selling tops and bottoms separately at $42-$49.

mechanisms.name: Size guide as a tabbed page with measurement diagrams and rules
mechanisms.description: The size guide is one page with tabs (Swim, Women's Apparel, Men's Apparel), a single XS-XXL table (Bust, Underbust/Bandwidth, Cup Size, Waist, Hips, inches), image diagrams marking where to measure, three one-line how-to-measure instructions, a between-sizes rule ("we suggest sizing up"), a caveat that some styles run small/large, a returns reassurance line and a sizing-help email. The PDP links to it with "VIEW SIZE GUIDE" on the same row as the "SIZE:" label.
mechanisms.why_it_works: Putting the rule, the diagram, the returns policy and the help contact on one screen answers the sizing question and de-risks it in the same place; the link placement next to the size selector catches the shopper at the moment of doubt.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Build a single S-XL guide with Bust, Underbust, Waist, Hips in inches and cm, one line per measurement, a clear between-sizes rule, a per-piece note for mesh and bandeau fits, and the exchange policy on the same page. Place "Size guide" inline beside the size buttons on every PDP and open it as a drawer rather than a new page.

mechanisms.name: Homepage as a router, prices held back to the grid
mechanisms.description: The homepage shows no product prices. It is a stack of image-led blocks each with one headline and one CTA: announcement bar (one campaign link) -> "New In" carousel with "SEE ALL" -> pairs block -> bento category tiles (Swimwear, Accessories, Beachwear, One Pieces) -> rewards block -> UGC feed ("Tag us @blackboughswim") -> newsletter -> footer.
mechanisms.why_it_works: The homepage sells the world and the entry points; price comparison is deferred to the collection page where cards are uniform. Each block having exactly one CTA keeps decision load low.
mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Use the homepage to route into three doors (Sunchild, Moonchild, Classics) plus a "New In" strip and a UGC block, each with a single CTA. Keep prices off the homepage and consistent on the shop grid. Piura's smaller range means fewer blocks: five sections maximum.

mechanisms.name: Reassurance lines placed directly under the buy box
mechanisms.description: Immediately below the size selector the PDP shows two fixed lines, each with a policy link: "Express International Shipping starts at $18. Fast, Reliable Shipping Worldwide." and "FREE returns for store credit 30 days from date of receipt." The cart drawer repeats "Free shipping on orders over $100 ● Easy returns".

mechanisms.applies_to_piura: Add two short lines under Piura's add-to-cart: the US shipping cost or free-shipping threshold, and the exchange/return window in plain words. Repeat the threshold in the cart drawer with a progress line ("$X away from free shipping") since a top plus bottom at $42-$49 each lands near a natural threshold.

mechanisms.name: Tag-driven badges and sale renaming
mechanisms.description: Card badges come from tags ("badge_new", "badge_pre-order"); sale SKUs are retitled with a " FINAL SALE" suffix and carry a compare_at price; availability is tracked per size variant (XS-XXL) so sold-out sizes are known per SKU; pre-order ship dates are written into the description.

mechanisms.name: Coverage and support stated in a fixed vocabulary inside the description
